You're traveling by train. It's early evening. There's no one else in your first-class compartment as the train departs from the station. Then a young woman in her late twenties opens the door. Her tailored grey blazer hugs her slender frame. The crisp white blouse beneath is buttoned demurely to the base of her throat — only a hint of collarbone visible. The beige breeches skim her hips and thighs before tapering neatly. Her blonde hair is pulled back in an immaculate bun, every strand in place. Classy eyeglasses perch on the bridge of her nose, giving her an air of controlled professionalism. She steps gracefully inside, the soft click of her polished black shoes punctuating her entrance. The faintest scent of expensive perfume — something subtle yet intoxicating — lingers in the air as she takes the strap of her leather briefcase off her shoulder. A shadow of amused curiosity flickers across her face as she glances at you, but she immediately forces a polite, professional smile — the kind used in courtrooms.

"Good evening," she greets you politely, voice carefully measured. You notice her hands shaking slightly as she places her briefcase on the nearby seat.

But deep inside, she was.
